title: Binary data & typed arrays
lede: Raw byte buffers and the typed views over them, the layer every networking, crypto, and file-I/O path is built on. Every typed array is a general expression and knows its `.buffer` and `.byteOffset`. ArrayBuffer, DataView, SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics, and a real bigint-backed BigInt64Array/DataView 64-bit path are all here, so binary layouts round-trip byte-exactly, an embedded NUL included.

entries.name: ArrayBuffer
entries.description: A fixed-length, zero-initialized (calloc'd) raw byte buffer, with .byteLength and .slice(start?, end?) (a copy, with array-slice negative-index/clamping rules). Unlike the TypedArrays below, it's a general expression — it works anywhere, not just in a variable declaration's initializer.

params.name: byteLength
params.desc: Size of the buffer in bytes.

entries.name: Uint8Array / Int8Array / Uint16Array / Int16Array / Uint32Array / Int32Array / Float32Array / Float64Array
entries.statusRow: Uint8Array / Int8Array / Uint16Array / Int16Array / Uint32Array / Int32Array / Float32Array / Float64Array
entries.description: Typed views over bytes, in three construction forms: a size (own new zero-filled buffer), an existing ArrayBuffer (a view sharing the same memory — writes through one view are visible through any other view over the same buffer, including a differently-typed one), the sub-range form new XArray(buf, byteOffset, length?), or a number[]/array literal/another TypedArray (a copy). Indexing, .length, the whole number[] HOF/iterator surface, plus the TypedArray-specific .set(source, offset?), .subarray(start?, end?) (a view, not a copy), .byteLength, and .buffer/.byteOffset (a view answers the buffer it was made over; an array with its own storage answers an ArrayBuffer made on first read and kept). Non-clamped writes wrap mod 2^width, matching real JS. Construction is a general expression — usable as a function argument, return value, object field, or method-chain head, not only a variable declaration's initializer.

returns.desc: A typed view or an own buffer.

entries.name: BigInt64Array / BigUint64Array
entries.description: 64-bit typed arrays whose elements are stored as raw i64/u64 but cross the language boundary as real arbitrary-precision bigint handles — writes require a bigint (a plain number is the spec's TypeError), reads wrap losslessly, so values above 2^53 round-trip exactly. Atomics load/store/RMW/compareExchange work on them, lowered to the same seq_cst i64 atomics.
differences: Only an explicit method allow-list is supported — indexing r/w, `.length`/`.byteLength`, `.at`, `.set`, `.subarray`, `.slice`, `.fill`, `.reverse`, for-of, `Atomics.*`; everything else (`.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce`/`.indexOf`/`.sort`/`.join`/iterator objects/…) is a compile-time rejection, never a raw-scalar leak

entries.name: Uint8ClampedArray
entries.description: A Uint8Array whose write path uses the spec's ToUint8Clamp instead of wrapping — values clamp to [0,255], floats round half to even (254.5 → 254, 255.5 → 255), and NaN → 0, on every write (element assignment including compound, construction, .set, .fill, and .map's result store). Reads are plain u8, so the entire read-side method surface works unchanged.
entries.snippet:
const clamped = new Uint8ClampedArray([-1, 300, 254.5, 255.5])
console.log(clamped[0], clamped[1], clamped[2], clamped[3]) // 0 255 254 255

entries.name: DataView
entries.description: Endian-controlled binary access over an ArrayBuffer: full get/set × Int8..Uint32/Float16/Float32/Float64 and BigInt64/BigUint64 (real bigint values, unsigned above 2^63 correct) with the spec's per-call littleEndian flag (default big-endian), plus .byteLength/.byteOffset/.buffer (an aliasing-identical ArrayBuffer). V8's RangeErrors on out-of-bounds access and construction, and V8's inspect output. It is a Blob part and a TextDecoder input like any BufferSource.

entries.name: Blob
entries.description: An immutable binary value with a MIME type, built from any iterable of strings, buffers, views and Blobs. The type is lowercased (or empty when not printable ASCII), and endings: 'native' converts line ends. Exposes .size/.type, .slice(start?, end?, contentType?) (a copy; type never inherited, per spec), .text()/.arrayBuffer()/.bytes() settling as Node's reader settles them, and .stream() → ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, one chunk per part.

entries.name: SharedArrayBuffer
entries.description: Identical representation to ArrayBuffer (all view constructions, .byteLength, .slice() — which returns a new SharedArrayBuffer, per spec — and DataView work unchanged), but postMessage/workerData/structuredClone share it by reference instead of deep-copying, the spec's semantics — and a view over it crosses as a view over the same memory. The backing memory for cross-thread Atomics.
differences: `grow(n)` requires the `{maxByteLength}` construction option (a compile-time rejection otherwise, where the spec throws a TypeError at run time); the maximum is reserved upfront

entries.name: Atomics
entries.description: load/store/add/sub/and/or/xor/exchange/compareExchange on any integer TypedArray including BigInt64Array/BigUint64Array (bigint operands/results), lowered directly to seq_cst LLVM atomics; float TypedArrays are a compile-time rejection. wait(ta, i, expected, timeoutMs?) returns "ok"/"not-equal"/"timed-out"; notify(ta, i, count?) returns the wake count — a portable futex substitute. Atomics.isLockFree(n) is true for 1/2/4/8.
differences: `wait` blocks the whole calling thread (event loop and fibers included) — allowed on the main thread (Node posture); no `waitAsync`
Index is bounds-unchecked, matching ordinary TypedArray indexing

entries.name: Node Buffer (Buffer.from/.alloc/.toString(encoding)/.write/etc.)
entries.description: A Buffer IS a Uint8Array — indexing, .length, .slice/.subarray, numeric .fill/.indexOf/.includes, HOFs, for-of, .set, .byteLength, and fs.writeFileSync(buffer) all share the TypedArray machinery; Buffer.from(...)/.alloc(...) are general expressions (call syntax, no vardecl restriction). Codecs both directions — utf8, utf16le/ucs2, hex, base64, base64url, latin1/binary/ascii — plus full read/write{U}Int{8,16,32}{LE,BE} + Float/Double + BigInt64/BigUInt64 accessors with catchable RangeError bounds checks.
entries.snippet:
const hello = Buffer.from("Hello");            // utf8 bytes
console.log(Buffer.from("4869", "hex").toString())      // Hi
console.log(hello.toString("base64"))          // SGVsbG8=
const pkt = Buffer.alloc(12)
pkt.writeBigInt64BE(9007199254740993n, 4)
differences: String-valued `.indexOf`/`.includes`/`.lastIndexOf` search the needle's UTF-8 bytes, and `.fill(string, offset?, end?)` repeats the needle's bytes (all no byteOffset/encoding); no 4-arg `.write(string, offset, length, encoding)` form; no `.swap16/32/64`, `.toJSON`, `Buffer.of`, `Buffer.isAscii`/`Buffer.isUtf8`, arbitrary-width `readIntLE(offset, byteLength)`, `poolSize`
